glosses: To do nothing in particular; to be idle.

examples.text: “I think it’s simply marvellous,” enthused Joyce, into the mirror, “that I’ve been able to adjust so quickly to office routine, don’t you? . . . After all these years of indulging myself, sleeping late, pottering, lazing about! […]”

glosses: To spend (time) idly but pleasantly.

examples.text: We whiled away the hours playing cards.

Heaven knows what pains the author has been at, what bitter experiences he has endured and what heartache suffered, to give some chance reader a few hours' relaxation or to while away the tedium of a journey.

glosses: To elapse, to pass.

examples.text: The rest of the night hours whiled away for the prisoners as few slept.
